explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly compares GPT-4 LLM judgments against human evaluation results for the Multi-turn Dialogue Induction task, reporting quantitative agreement metrics

prompts.notes: Full prompts provided in Appendix A.2 for both Multi-turn Dialogue Induction and Fairness-Factuality Balance tasks, including specific evaluation criteria

guidelines.notes: Detailed quality control questions and annotation guidelines provided in Appendices A-B

sample_size.notes: Randomly selected 10% of FEIs (256 out of 2568 instances) for GPT-4 vs human comparison

quantitative_scores.notes: Agreement rate between GPT-4 and human evaluators on Multi-turn Dialogue Induction task

validation_results.summary_finding: GPT-4 achieved 97.27% agreement with human evaluators, demonstrating strong reliability as an LLM judge for fairness evaluation

criteria_mapping.notes: Human evaluators assessed broader data quality aspects, while LLM focused on fairness violations in specific tasks; both evaluated bias-related criteria
